summary.text: A patient with thyroid eye disease received prolonged peribulbar triamcinolone treatment, eight injections in each orbit. One week after completing the eight injections the patient complained of fatigue, intense weakness and headache, and experienced an episode of syncope.

The patient was referred to an endocrinologist, who diagnosed adrenal insufficiency based on the low basal levels of blood cortisol. The patient was treated with oral hydrocortisone. No later course or cortisol values are reported for this patient.

article_limitations: Retrospective case series of 123 patients with thyroid eye disease treated with peribulbar triamcinolone; five singly described series members are rostered (p1 hyperglycemia, p2 adrenal insufficiency, p3 ocular hypertension, p4 the operated DON patient with decreased vision, p5 discontinuation after eyelid ecchymosis). Roster is incomplete (5 of 123); overlap between p3/p4 and p1/p2 is not stated.

Cohort statistics (Table 1 demographics, Table 2 complication counts, injection counts, response rates, discussion of cited studies) are aggregate and are not copied to individuals; only explicit all-of-group statements (all 123 had TED and PT; all eleven needing other treatment received systemic corticosteroids; all operated patients improved visual field and color test; RAPD in 4/4; all ecchymoses resolved spontaneously) are applied. Pairs and groups (two with diplopia worsening, nine with ecchymosis) are not rostered.

Cohort arithmetic inconsistencies: "one patient; 1.6%" for the two systemic complications; "Eleven (8.5%)" for 11 of 123; Table 1 severity percentages do not match their counts. None is attributed to an individual.
No age, laboratory values, doses beyond injection counts, or dates are given for any rostered patient. The source has no figures and no supplementary material (raw XML checked).
